subject: SableTech: sudden p95 latency jump on sable-zeta-9.2 — escalation/rollback request
messages:
From: Alex Munroe <alex.munroe@sabletech.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@sabletech.com
Date: 2028-06-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: p95 latency spike since model sable-zeta-9.2 rollout

Karthik,

We started seeing a sharp p95 increase on our production traffic after rolling the sable-zeta-9.2 variant at 08:30 UTC. Dashboard shows p95 climbed from ~180ms to ~1.15s for the last 30m; error-rate is stable ( <0.1% ). This is impacting our interactive search UX.

Quick facts:
- rollout window: 08:30–08:45 UTC, gradual 10% increments
- impacted route: /api/v1/search (long-context prompts)
- sample request ids: req_6642, req_6649 (attached traces)

Can you confirm whether this is known and whether we can be reverted to the previous variant? We need a rollback if this persists.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Munroe
SRE Lead, SableTech

Attachments: svc_trace_20280610.json, p95_trend_20280610.png

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Alex Munroe <alex.munroe@sabletech.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-10T09:25:00Z
Subject: Re: p95 latency spike since model sable-zeta-9.2 rollout

Alex — thanks for the quick heads-up. I see the charts you attached. I'm escalating immediately to infra/serving.

Immediate asks:
1) Rishi / Marissa / Neha: can you validate whether the rollout triggered a kernel/path that increases attention compute for long-contexts? Check recent kernel selection logs and the routing policy for sable-zeta-9.2.
2) Ops: please prepare a rollback plan for the variant and the exact traffic cut-over steps (we'll need a canary revert + 5m watch window).

If we determine this is model-induced (not infra), I'm going to request an emergency variant rollback for SableTech only. Alex — please stand by for an ETA.

Karthik
VP, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment notes: I saw svc_trace_20280610.json — will upload to the incident folder shortly.

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-10T11:30:00Z
Subject: RE: p95 latency spike since model sable-zeta-9.2 rollout

Quick triage notes (11:30 UTC):
- Reproduced p95 increase on local replay of SableTech traffic using the sable-zeta-9.2 binary. Tail tokens dominate, KV-cache hit pattern unchanged; CPU on host is normal.
- Kernel selector picked the new large-mem attention path for sequences >1.2k tokens; that path has 20–30% higher single-request latency but improves peak throughput.
- Fallback variant (sable-zeta-9.1-quant) is available and compatible with SableTech config.

Options:
A) Per-customer rollback to sable-zeta-9.1 for SableTech (fastest: route rule + variant pin at 100% for their tenant).
B) Toggle routing to prefer legacy attention kernel (requires a short restart of the serving pool, 3–5m disruption).
C) Enable temporary traffic cap at 30% for long-context requests until a perf patch lands.

Recommend A for lowest user impact. I'll draft the rollback steps and a canary plan.

Rishi
Sr. Infra Engineer

Attachments: mutational_diff.log (internal), planned_rollback_steps.txt

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Munroe <alex.munroe@sabletech.com>
Date: 2028-06-10T15:50:00Z
Subject: Escalation: need leadership approval for SLA carve-out or immediate rollback

Karthik — legal and CS are asking for guidance. SableTech is on a committed contract with a 99.95% latency SLO for interactive endpoints. If we rollback-only for them, we remain within usual operational changes. If we delay rollback and apply a carve-out (temporary SLA tolerance) we need an exec sign-off documenting the window and credits.

Decision options for exec:
- Approve per-customer rollback (no customer credits, temporary traffic disruption <5m).
- Approve SLA carve-out: window 09:00–17:00 UTC, grant partial credit if p95 exceeds threshold for >2 hours (not recommended unless rollback carries risk).

Alex — what is your preference? Karthik, can you confirm that rollback is expected to restore p95 to baseline based on Rishi's replay? If yes, I'll prepare the change request and notify Legal/CS with the rollback timeline.

Marissa
Head of Product Ops

---
Attachment: mutual_action_plan.docx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Munroe <alex.munroe@sabletech.com>, operations@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-10T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Escalation: need leadership approval for SLA carve-out or immediate rollback

Team — authorize per-customer rollback for SableTech to sable-zeta-9.1. Rationale: replay shows median and p95 revert on 9.1; rollback minimizes customer impact and avoids SLA carve-out which sets a bad precedent. Execute the canary at 16:50 UTC:

Plan:
- 16:50 UTC: Pin SableTech routing to sable-zeta-9.1 at 100% (apply via routing rule)
- 16:50–16:55 UTC: Monitor p95 + errors; if stable, keep for 1h then coordinate with SableTech for a full fleet variant change next maintenance window
- Post-mortem: eng to produce root cause and perf patch; PM to coordinate customer comms and any required credits (unlikely).

Alex — please confirm on your side once you see p95 return to baseline. I'll file the change and notify Legal/CS that rollback is the chosen path.

Karthik
VP, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference

---
Status: rollback authorized; tracking: JIRA-INC-5541
